candidates.evidence: CRD DFT match (row 1571, mp-23218, scale 1.023) explains 4 of 5 fitted bands: 79.6 (Eg, ref 80.0), 104.5 (Eg, ref 105.0), 120.3 (Ag, ref 118.4), 165.8 (Eg, ref 167.9); score 0.77 is the highest of the library candidates. Unexplained: 668.1 (judged noise, see peaks). Missing predicted Ag at 61.7 cm-1 (rel. int. 0.14) lies at the 60 cm-1 low-shift edge of the data. No experimental AsI3 Raman reference was available in the tools, so confidence is moderate and not literature-confirmed. AsI3 is a molecular crystal rather than a classic layered vdW material, which conflicts with the task's premise.

CRD match (row 4740) assigns A1g to 104.4 and 120.5 cm-1 only; leaves 79.6 and 165.8 unexplained, so the score (0.60) is well below AsI3. Included because HgI2 is a layered vdW halide and is the most plausible layered alternative in the library.
CRD match (row 4251) covers 79.6 (E2), 104.5 (E2), 120.3 (A1) only; leaves 165.8 unexplained; score 0.57.
CRD match (row 4232) covers 104.5 (A1g) and 120.3 (Eg); predicts a strong unobserved A1g at 139.6 cm-1; score 0.45.
CRD match (row 3526) covers 104.5 (B3g) and 120.3 (Ag) only; predicts strong unobserved Ag modes at 60.9 and 147.5 cm-1; score 0.33.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint is null), so there is no stated material to verify. Identification is from the spectrum alone: a DFT-based library match (Computational Raman Database) on the four strong bands 79.6, 104.5, 120.3 and 165.8 cm-1. No curated literature mode table exists for AsI3 in the skill library (lookup_reference_modes returned no entry), so the assignment is library-based rather than literature-confirmed.

limits: Identification rests only on a DFT library match (Computational Raman Database). No experimental AsI3 Raman reference was compared, and no literature search was run, so the top candidate is not literature-confirmed. Confidence for AsI3 is moderate (0.5).

The task says the material is layered (van der Waals), but AsI3 is a molecular crystal and HgI2 is the only layered candidate in the matches. Both are weaker matches. The spectrum cannot settle the premise; a structure check or an independent reference is needed.
Mode labels (Ag vs Eg) are DFT labels. The spectrum is a single unpolarized measurement, so no polarization test (rl.py classify_polarization) can confirm the irreps.

Predicted Ag at 61.7 cm-1 (relative intensity 0.14) is not resolved. The data start at 60 cm-1 and the low-shift region is dominated by the Rayleigh tail and baseline, so this mode can neither be confirmed nor excluded. The 79.6 cm-1 band fit (FWHM 6.5 cm-1) may be affected by the baseline.

The 668.1 cm-1 fitted band is at the noise level and is not treated as a real mode. Its width (1.35 cm-1) is narrower than the other bands, and its neighbourhood is erratic. A contaminant or a real weak mode cannot be fully excluded without a cleaner spectrum.
Signal-to-noise is low (strongest band 18 x noise), and the spectrum has many zero-valued points above about 500 cm-1. Weak modes above 200 cm-1 may be missed.

Measured positions carry fit errors of 0.2 to 0.5 cm-1. No Si calibration line is present, so the absolute wavenumber calibration is unchecked. The DFT frequency scale (x1.023) adds about 2% uncertainty to the assignments.
Laser at 532 nm: no check was done on whether resonance with an electronic transition of AsI3 or HgI2 changes the relative intensities.
Sample identity, purity, and thickness are unknown. No substrate was given or detected, so no substrate lines are reported.
